media.fallback: alternate exact project/provider homes; never fabricated images, screenshots, data URLs, or base64 galleries
media.scheduling: provider-adaptive all-source parallelism: every canonical source home is admitted; each provider selects the minimum complete-response keeper(s), while redundant physically cancellable Node/Chromium streams stop after first trusted media. Measured pooled Rust drains are not launched as broad redundant probes. Adaptive main-process prime target remains wide and no project/gallery/result cap is introduced.
media.galleryCap: none; exact discovered HTTP(S) image URLs are deduplicated but not truncated
media.transport: provider-adaptive transport policy: Chromium is the complete keeper for login/session-heavy sources; Node is the complete keeper for static SSR/API-friendly providers; CurseForge retains Chromium + vendored wreq Rust as complementary complete keepers. Tiny public API seeds race canonical pages where available. BuiltByBit is browser-navigation-only without an official authenticated API token. Redundant pooled native tails are not sprayed across every provider.
media.connectionWarmup: One registry preconnects provider and media origins across all 23 first-class families plus their known CDNs/API seeds before first card paint; cached discovered origins are added without record caps.
media.identityPolicy: exact project title/slug/canonical identity; collection/shop/profile pages resolve an exact child project before gallery media is accepted
media.previewPolicy: cards may use a smaller real provider srcset candidate for faster first paint; hover zoom and lightbox always upgrade to the full original provider URL; no gallery item or original-resolution URL is capped or discarded
media.deepDiscovery: reuses a warm adaptive 6-10 WebContentsView pool; login/session-heavy and browser-only providers receive an immediate/near-immediate DOM-ready hedge, while static/API-friendly providers stay on streamed HTML unless visible fast paths miss
media.indexFetchDedup: shared Planet Minecraft/AFDIAN/Fourthwall/BOOTH provider index URLs are single-flighted and reused from a short-lived byte-budgeted raw-document cache; an early body-prefix gate can resolve an exact child before the full index completes; persistent media cache remains context-scoped and uncapped by record count
media.indexSeed: high-confidence exact child links may supply their own real provider src/srcset image immediately; exact child-page discovery still enriches the full uncapped gallery
media.firstPaint: batched context-aware cache hydrate -> all canonical source homes start -> tiny public API seed races where available -> provider policy launches minimum complete keeper(s) plus cancellable first-media probes -> first identity-validated real provider image paints -> image CDN is preconnected/warmed in the same Chromium session -> uncapped rich gallery/author discovery remains available on demand
media.startup: one batched cache hydrate -> atomic all-project frontier admission -> multi-provider origin preconnect -> provider-adaptive parallel source racing -> progressive first-media paint; no project/gallery/result caps and no synthetic imagery
media.modrinthBulkPrime: all unique Modrinth slugs are fetched through official GET /v2/projects?ids=[…] batches sized only by safe encoded-URL length; every requested project is preserved and subsequent team/author/gallery enrichment remains available

providerUniverse.genericFallback: unknown exact HTTP(S) provider pages still use identity-checked OG/JSON-LD/DOM discovery; no provider homepage is substituted for a known exact project URL
providerUniverse.authenticatedSources: Patreon/AFDIAN/other login-sensitive pages keep the persistent Chromium session as complete-response authority; credentials are never copied into catalog data. Browser-only policies do not bypass paid/private access.
providerUniverse.publicMetadataSeeds: SpigotMC via public Spiget resource metadata, Hangar via public project API/avatar, GitLab via public project avatar metadata. Seeds are non-exclusive and never replace canonical live gallery enrichment.
providerUniverse.browserOnly: BuiltByBit uses real persistent Chromium navigation without an official authenticated API token; direct Node/wreq/impit scraping lanes are disabled.

bandwidthAudit.method: real localhost TCP streams through production Node + vendored wreq + vendored impit transports; early trusted Patreon media URL followed by a 1 MiB deliberately slow tail
bandwidthAudit.finding: wreq/impit logical body abort can continue draining pooled network bodies; 2.5 disables them as broad redundant probes instead of pretending cancellation saved bandwidth
bandwidthAudit.expectedPolicy: one complete keeper + physically cancellable probe(s) instead of every transport draining every provider page tail

runtimeFixes.nativeChromeCompositor: dedicated topmost native WebContentsView for titlebar/toolbar; remote website views stay underneath; active attached views resize in place and are never hide/re-shown by focus guards
runtimeFixes.remoteInputFocus: remote WebContents focus and root-shell blur use paint-only guards; permission/dialog close restores focus to active content
runtimeFixes.browserBottomEdge: browser/catalog/split content reserves only the protected bottom status surface (28px expanded or 10px collapsed); no unprotected BrowserWindow footer remains
runtimeFixes.byteStringCrash: Google authenticated programmatic source transfers remain on the ByteString-safe pooled Node transport with Chromium cookies bridged per redirect; public live-media provider pages may additionally race Electron session.fetch and vendored Rust wreq because they do not pass through the former Google/Undici header-crash path.
runtimeFixes.nativeSplitter: dedicated 18px protected WebContentsView above both native panes; screen-coordinate pointer drag, pointer capture, keyboard resize, 50/50 reset and side swap
runtimeFixes.nativeModalIsolation: site permissions use native Electron message boxes; Catalog Center is a dedicated child BrowserWindow; clear-data confirmation is native; top chrome is hard-capped at 430px and never becomes a full-window modal/input shield
runtimeFixes.nativeWindowErgonomics: frameless window explicitly retains Windows WS_THICKFRAME resize/snap behavior; empty tab-strip/titlebar space and non-interactive bottom status space are native drag regions while tabs/buttons remain no-drag controls
